sections.text: न तदस्ति पृथिव्यां वा दिवि देवेषु वा पुनः।
There is nothing anywhere on earth or in the higher worlds which is free from the three Qualities - for they are born of Nature.
O Arjuna! The duties of spiritual teachers, the soldiers, the traders and the servants have all been fixed according to the dominant Quality in their nature.
Serenity, self-restraint, austerity, purity, forgiveness, as well as uprightness, knowledge, wisdom and faith in God - these constitute the duty of a spiritual Teacher.

Chapter 18, Moksha Sanyasa Yoga. This is obviously the last chapter in our studies of Bhagavad Gita. So we had been systematically studying Bhagavad Gita.
The goal of that is to figure out how I should act in this world so that I can get the maximum happiness. So we have first understood who we are in the Bhagavad Gita as individuals, how we function in this world. And then we have also talked about who is that? Who has the control over this entire universe and therefore also over my life.
We are coming to the end portion of the Bhagavad Gita. We are synthesizing this knowledge about who we are at the individual level. What is my relationship with this world and the Supreme Being? But the bottom line still remains, how can I be happy? So in this chapter we are analyzing the factors affecting my actions and the outcome of my actions.
So in the beginning, Arjun asked what is sannyas and what is thyaga? Because in all this discussion I picked up these two words which ultimately lead to happiness, ultimately leads you to liberation, freedom from all the sorrows and unhappiness. So I want to understand these two concepts so I can find out how I can act in this world. Number one, very simply said, giving up all desire prompted actions is Sanyas.
If you can reach a point where you dont have to do anything to satisfy your desires, then you are a sannyasi. That can only happen when I have exhausted all the desire. There is no desire left.
Therefore I dont have to act for my desires. That can only happen if I have no ego and no individual identification. Sarva Karma Falatyagama stagger.
That seems like the goal one can strive for that I can probably work on Tyaga part. But because the Tyaga can be misunderstood, giving up, abandoning something can be misunderstood. We went into discussion about this. Tyaga also can be of three types.
This Prakriti has three qualities, so anything associated with the Prakriti will have the same Triguna. We used the example before that every gold ornament will have the same ingredient of gold. Gold ornaments also come in different carats -- 18 carat versus 16 carat, 12 carat, 24 carat.
What that means is something else is mixed into the gold. You cannot make an ornament out of pure gold; they have to add zinc. The proportion of that metal can change, but every gold ornament will have both gold and zinc, which makes it more malleable, more workable.
It is the proportion which makes it 12 carat vs 18 carat vs 24 carat. Prakriti is also like that. The first thing that comes to mind is I should give up all my actions. So we reaffirmed that action cannot be given up by anybody.
It is not possible for a living being to completely abandon all actions. Therefore, now we need to understand what actions are to be abandoned. In the beginning, Bhagawan gave an indication -- desire prompted actions.
So what actions should I perform? Yajna Dana Tapa should not be given up at any cost. The actions which are purifying your mind and intellect, they should be performed. And then we talked about the anatomy of action, because we are going to be focused on actions all our life.
We are going to be focusing on how I should act in the right manner and what actions are to be abandoned. We looked at three propellers of actions. The knowledge, Gnanam, Gnem, Parignatha -- the knowledge, the knower, and the knowable.
We also looked at Karanam, Karma, Karta, iti, Trivedha, Karma, Sangraha. Action only comes into existence if these three are there: the instrument of action, the doer, and the action itself. Then we analyzed that Gnana, Karma, and Karta also can be of three types. Anything which is part of the Prakriti will have the same three ingredients in different proportions.
Gnana, Karma, and Karta also come in three types. We also discussed Buddhi and Dhruti -- the foundation of any action, my intellect and my fortitude. These basically make any action possible, or rather, success in any action possible.
Even those two can come in three different varieties. And in the end our goal was to get Sukham, happiness or Ananda. See this Sukha also can be three types.
Sattvik, Sukha, which is at the beginning seems like a poison. But in the end it is like a nectar. Work hard to get somewhere.
But when you get there, there is joy there. So thats a Sattvik sukha. It seems good in the beginning, but in the end it gives pain.
Thats Rajasik sukha. So the pleasures in life which we pursue, they are like Rajasik sukha. It gives you some joy, but in the end it gives you unhappiness.
Even going on vacation -- every time you come back, you say, Im tired, I cant do anything. I need a vacation from my vacation, you know. So every pleasure which we seek in the end it ends them into some kind of a misery. So the Bhagawan says, thats Rajasik sukha.
It starts as very pleasant, ends in unpleasantness. And Tamasik sukha? It is not enjoyable in the beginning, and also not enjoyable in the end. Scratching, for example -- when we start, its not really that pleasant.
And after you are done with it, it is also very painful. This is why Bhagavan said thats Tamasik sukha. And then we are coming to the segment where Bhagavan said, therefore now understand that everything in this Prakriti is made up of these three gunas.
So human beings are also affected by these three gunas. These three gunas affect all the people we come across and ourselves. And based on those gunas, they can be also classified into Sattvik, Rajasic and Tamasic.
But we may get confused. The Bhagawan makes it clear that it is not possible for anything or any being in this Prakriti to be without these three gunas. All three gunas have to be present for a thing or being to exist in space and time.
For something to exist in space and time, it has to have inertia. Without inertia, the thing simply cannot persist -- otherwise it vanishes the moment its created. Somebody gave an example -- I think it was who gave a story of Brahmaji when he first created human beings.
They were all completely Sattvik. As soon as Brahmaji created them, they all went back to their true nature. Brahmaji was really baffled.
How can I keep this thing stable? The inertia tamas makes things remain in this time and space. But the thing also cannot remain what it is. And it rajast with activities.
We now know from science that even atom which seems stable has intense activity in it. All electrons are circling around that neutral proton. And the thing needs to know that it exists, which is Sattva.
So Sattva, Rajas, and Tamas -- I exist, I act, and I remain in my place. These three are absolutely necessary for anything or any being to be in existence. So the verses which we are coming to now clarify: Na tad asthi prithivyam va divi deveshu va punah Sattvam prakritei muktaha yat yabhi sha tribhirgunaihi -- on this earth and also in the heavens among Devas, there is not a single being who is free from all these three gunas.
Thinking of yourself without these three gunas is not possible. But at the same time, we keep hearing Bhagavan say Guna teet Bhava Arjuna. We probably understood that I should go beyond this guna, so I should get rid of all three gunas.
Bhagawan said that is not possible. You can stop identifying with this Guna. So my mind is working in Tamasic mode or Rajasic mode.
I should be able to introspect and say its my mind which is a rajasic mode. If I can make him go to Sattvic mode, it will be more comfortable. But if I identify with my mind, am I obviously identifying with my mind and intellect? So you can be Gunateet only if you are not identifying with your limited self.
Bhagavan said, be clear that these three gunas are present in all beings -- divine beings and also the mortals on this planet. They all are affected by these three gunas. And therefore all humanity and all beings can be classified into Sattvik, Rajasik, and Tamasik depending on their predominant qualities. Brahman, Kshatriya, Vishyam, Shudranamcha, Parantpa, Karmani, Pravibakthani, Swabhava, Prabhavai Gunai.
This is basically a clarification for all of us who have this confusion about what is this caste system. Bhagavan created Brahman, Vishyanshudra and therefore now you are bound by this divisions. It clearly says that Karmani, Pravibakthani, Swabhava, Prabhavai Gunaihe.
Their duties are divided among this Brahmakshatriya, Vaishna Sudra for their own nature, Prabhavayi Gunai hi. According to their own nature, their duties are determined for Brahma, Vaishya, Kshudra and Kshatriya. So it is your own nature which makes you Brahman or Kshatri or Shudra or Vaishya.
Bhagavan makes it clear here: it is not by birth, not by association, not by caste, creed, or color, but by the texture of your mind and intellect. Your gunas will make you the Brahma, Kshatriya, Vishya, or Sudra. Shamah, Damah, Tapaha, Shaucham, Kshantihi, Arjamam, Evacha, Gnanam, Vignanam, Astikyam, Brahma Karma, Swabhavajam.
First he said their duties in life are attributed to them according to their own nature. You have to give a person work or his place in your company, in your society and community based on what his aptitude is. Thats why before going to college you take an aptitude test.
Even in a company, two engineers come. One may be more research oriented and other may be more practical oriented. You put them in right place.
In our profession it is much more clearer that we are all architects. But some are more design oriented so they can design, some more creative. Some are more technical minded so they can put things together in a building a little better.
And some are more into administrative. Make sure that things are done right. So we used to have three divisions in companies.
There used to go to design department, Production department and Construction Administration department. Suppose more glamorous because its creative. But depending on your aptitude, you end up going from one to the another.
Sometimes, even if you dont have the aptitude, you think, Because design is more glamorous, I want to go there. But then you would be miserable because you wont be able to perform your task properly. Eventually you end up going where your aptitude is whether you like it or not. Bhagawan said that the duties are distributed among them according to their own gunas.
Now how do I know what gunas Bhagavan says know what Brahmanas qualities are? Shamaha, control over the mind, mental control, Shamah Dhammah, physical control, control over your senses, Tapaha austerity. Any discipline which you follow, Shaucham, purity, Shantihi, forgiveness, Arjvam, straightforwardness. Whatever it is, you can see clearly: Gnanam, Vignanam -- knowledge and also applied knowledge, the application of knowledge.
Astikyam -- faith in the underlying truth that this world has its basis. We have learnt in Bhagavad Gita before that those people who are of devilish qualities think there is no basis in this world. The Bhagawan says Astikyam, that faith in the underlying truth, the underlying reality in this nature -- Brahma Karma Swabhavajam.
This comes naturally to Brahmins. In other words, the people who have these qualities are the Brahmins. Now, say you identified that you are that person.
You ask him to run a business. Obviously he is not good at it. So you cant really put somebody in charge of something he is not good at.

Verse 40 makes a universal declaration: nothing in this world, neither on earth nor among the celestial beings, is free from the three gunas born of Prakriti. This is both humbling and liberating. Humbling because no one can claim to be beyond these qualities while living in a body. Liberating because it means we should not despair at finding these tendencies in ourselves - they are the nature of existence. The goal is not elimination but transcendence through dis-identification.
Verses 41-42 begin describing the four varnas based on svabhava-prabhava-guna - qualities born of ones own nature. This is not a birth-based caste system but a recognition that people have different temperaments and aptitudes. The Brahmana qualities are listed: shama (serenity), dama (self-control), tapa (austerity), saucha (purity), kshanti (forgiveness), arjava (straightforwardness), jnana (knowledge), vijnana (applied wisdom), and astikyam (faith in the underlying reality). These are not inherited but developed through inner work.
Reflect honestly: Which qualities from the Brahmana list do you embody naturally, and which require effort? The teaching is not that everyone should become a Brahmana but that everyone should discover and fulfill their own svadharma (inherent nature). Today, identify one quality from this list that you want to develop. Rather than forcing it, ask: What in my life is obstructing this quality? Shama (serenity) is obstructed by constant stimulation. Arjava (straightforwardness) is obstructed by fear of consequences. Address the obstruction, and the quality naturally emerges.
